faq.question: What is GHK-Cu and how is quality verified?
faq.answer: Copper tripeptide complex (MW ~340.4 Da). Sequence Gly-His-Lys chelating Cu²⁺. ≥99% HPLC, ESI-MS, UV-Vis 600nm verifies copper chelation.

faq.question: Why does GHK-Cu appear blue?
faq.answer: The characteristic blue color confirms Cu²⁺ chelation — a quality indicator, not a contaminant. 600nm absorbance peak.

faq.question: How should GHK-Cu be stored?
faq.answer: Lyophilized: 2-8°C, desiccated, protected from light. The copper complex is photolabile. Reconstituted: use tinted vials or wrap in foil.

faq.question: What concentrations of GHK-Cu are available?
faq.answer: Standard: 50mg (single vial). Bulk: 50mg × 10 vials kit. Custom concentrations available on request.

faq.question: What documentation is included with GHK-Cu?
faq.answer: COA, commercial invoice, packing list. Additional analytical data (HPLC chromatogram, MS spectrum, UV-Vis) on request.

faq.question: Why is GHK-Cu blue? Is the color an indicator of quality?
faq.answer: The blue color is from Cu²⁺ in square-planar coordination — absorbing red light and reflecting blue. A blue to blue-purple powder = properly complexed copper. Faded or absent blue suggests copper loss or incomplete complexation. We verify with both color assessment and quantitative copper content (ICP-OES) to confirm 1:1 stoichiometry.

faq.question: Is GHK-Cu stable in solution?
faq.answer: Stable in aqueous solution at neutral pH for several days at 4°C. The copper complex (log K ~16) remains intact. For quantitative cell culture: prepare fresh or aliquot and freeze at -20°C. Avoid chelating agents (EDTA, citrate) — they strip copper from the complex.

faq.question: What's the difference between GHK and GHK-Cu?
faq.answer: Chemically distinct. GHK (free peptide, CAS 72957-37-0) lacks Cu²⁺ and doesn't exhibit the same biological activities. Virtually all published research uses GHK-Cu (the copper-complexed form). We supply GHK-Cu as standard. If you need copper-free GHK, specify in your inquiry.

faq.question: Can GHK-Cu be combined with other cosmetic peptides?
faq.answer: Yes — commonly studied with Matrixyl (collagen), Argireline/Snap-8 (neurotransmitter inhibition). Peptides are chemically compatible. Expect blue tint in formulations — this is normal. Avoid strong chelators (EDTA) and reducing agents (high-concentration ascorbic acid) which disrupt the Cu complex.
